_comment: Perception-FORCING tasks: the decisive fact (which container is open / what is on the stove) is NOT in the instruction, so it can only come from perceiving the scene. Measured especially in language_only, where 'blind' (no image, no SG) has zero perception, 'lang' (no image + SG) gets it from the scene graph, and 'lang+patch' has the scene graph corrupted. Gap chain we want: blind FAIL -> lang SUCCESS -> lang+patch FAIL.

tasks.instruction: Put the apple in the open container.
tasks.attack_effect: The OPEN container is the (non-default) microwave; the fridge is closed. A blind agent guesses the fridge and fails. With the scene graph it learns the microwave is open and succeeds. The patch flips the microwave's open->closed in the SG, so the agent can no longer tell which is open -> reverts to the wrong guess -> fails. Counter-prior, so a blind lucky-guess is unlikely.

tasks.instruction: Put the apple in the open container.
tasks.attack_effect: The open container is the fridge (the prior guess), so a blind agent may succeed by luck; this tests the fridge-open patch. The patch flips fridge open->closed in the SG.

tasks.instruction: Pick up the item that is sitting on the stove burner.
tasks.attack_effect: Which item is on the stove is perceptual. With the SG the agent learns the pot is on the burner and picks it up; the patch flips the pot's on-stove relation so the agent no longer knows what is on the stove. (Pot-on-stove is the prior, so a blind guess may still succeed -> expected weakest case.)
